title: Trauma — Primary Survey, Hemorrhagic Shock & MTP
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: ATLS Primary Survey / Hemorrhagic Shock / Trauma Activation
ATLS 11th edition (2024); CRASH-2 (TXA); PROPPR (1:1:1 ratio); CDC/ACS-COT Field Triage Guidelines 2021

changelog.change: Initial entry — ABCDE with the immediate life-threats, hemorrhagic shock classification, the MTP (ratio, TXA, calcium, targets), TBI initial targets, and eFAST windows.

summary: ABCDE, addressing each life-threat as it's found. Control external haemorrhage first (direct pressure → tourniquet → wound packing). Permissive hypotension (SBP 80–90) until surgical control — EXCEPT in TBI, where you protect cerebral perfusion (MAP ≥ 80). Give blood in a 1:1:1 ratio and TXA within 3 hours.

rows: Jaw-thrust, suction, in-line stabilisation. Intubate if GCS ≤ 8 or the airway is threatened (burns, expanding neck haematoma). LEMON assessment.
Airway obstruction; unstable mid-face / laryngeal injury
Rate, SpO2, bilateral auscultation, tracheal position, chest wall.
Tension pneumothorax → needle decompression (2nd ICS MCL or 4th–5th ICS AAL) then finger/chest tube. Open pneumothorax → 3-sided occlusive dressing. Massive haemothorax. Flail chest.

2 large-bore IVs. Tourniquet + wound packing for extremity / junctional bleeding. eFAST. Pelvic binder for an unstable pelvis. Activate MTP for Class III–IV. Permissive hypotension (SBP 80–90) until surgical control — except TBI.
Uncontrolled haemorrhage (chest, abdomen, pelvis, long bones, 'floor and 4 more'); cardiac tamponade
GCS, pupils, gross motor; blood glucose. C-spine imaging per NEXUS / Canadian criteria.
Fully undress + log-roll; PREVENT hypothermia (warm room, warm fluids, blankets) — hypothermia is one leg of the lethal triad.

body.text: Young patients compensate and can look Class I–II until they crash — track the trend, the base deficit / lactate, and the response to the first unit of blood. A patient who only transiently responds to blood is still bleeding and needs the OR / IR.

Activate for uncontrolled haemorrhage needing ≥ 3 units RBC in 1 h, an ABC score ≥ 2, or anticipated ≥ 10 units / 24 h. Transfuse RBC : FFP : platelets in a 1:1:1 ratio (PROPPR). Whole blood if available. TXA 1 g IV over 10 min within 3 h of injury (CRASH-2), then 1 g over 8 h — giving TXA after 3 h is associated with harm. Calcium: 1 g CaCl₂ (or 3 g gluconate) after every ~4 units of RBC (citrate chelation → ionised hypocalcaemia worsens coagulopathy and cardiac function). Targets: fibrinogen > 150–200 mg/dL (cryoprecipitate / concentrate if low), platelets ≥ 50k (≥ 100k if TBI or ongoing bleeding), ionised calcium > 1.1, temperature > 36 °C, pH > 7.2.

items: MAP ≥ 80 mmHg (CPP ≥ 60) — a single episode of hypotension roughly doubles mortality in TBI.
PaCO2 35–45 mmHg. Brief hyperventilation to 30–35 ONLY as a bridge to definitive treatment in active herniation.
Herniation: head of bed 30°, head midline, mannitol 0.5–1 g/kg OR hypertonic saline 3% ~250 mL. GCS ≤ 8: intubate, consider an ICP monitor, neurosurgery.
Reverse anticoagulation urgently (4F-PCC + vitamin K for warfarin; idarucizumab for dabigatran).
RUQ (Morrison's pouch, hepatorenal) — the most sensitive abdominal window for free fluid.
LUQ (splenorenal recess) — fluid collects above the spleen and in the subphrenic space; harder to see.
Pelvis (rectovesical / pouch of Douglas) — scan with a full bladder if possible.
Subxiphoid (pericardial) — effusion / tamponade; assess the IVC alongside.

Bilateral anterior pleura — lung sliding present = no pneumothorax at that spot (~97% sensitive). Absent sliding → suspect pneumothorax; M-mode 'barcode / stratosphere' sign vs the normal 'seashore' sign; a lung point is pathognomonic.

body.text: Trauma team activation (CDC/ACS-COT field triage): highest-tier / trauma-centre transport for GCS ≤ 13, SBP < 90 (or < 110 if ≥ 65), RR < 10 or > 29, shock index > 1.0, any penetrating injury to head/neck/torso/proximal extremity, flail chest, ≥ 2 proximal long-bone fractures, crushed/degloved/mangled or amputated-proximal-to-wrist/ankle extremity, pelvic fracture, open/depressed skull fracture, or paralysis.

buildNote: Tier 1. The ABC score and a dedicated trauma-team-activation criteria module are natural companions. Pelvic-fracture management and REBOA are separate.
